headline: Steady inflows and wider margins; preferred buyback funded
summary_short: Adjusted EPS rose 18% y/y to $0.72 while GAAP EPS slipped 1.5% to $0.65. Net long-term inflows were $35.1B and ending AUM reached $2.54T, up 19.4% y/y.
summary_long: Net revenue rose 4% sequentially while operating expenses fell 1%, lifting adjusted operating margin to 40.7%. Inflows were led by ETFs and Index ($28.5B) and QQQ ($6.7B), with money market inflows of $52.9B; Fundamental Fixed Income and Fundamental Equities saw outflows. Net debt fell $393M and buybacks were $65M. On October 26 Invesco repurchased $1.5B of Series A Preferred from MassMutual using a five-year bank term loan, leaving $1B outstanding.
confidence_notes: Adjusted figures are non-GAAP. Net long-term flows in the quarter include QQQ following its December 2025 restructuring, so y/y comparisons differ in basis. GAAP net income fell 2.3% y/y.

drivers.explanation: Q3 inflows of $35.1B versus $45.1B in Q2; ETFs and Index, QQQ, Multi-Asset/Other and China JV led, partly offset by outflows in Fundamental Fixed Income, Fundamental Equities and Private Markets.
Net revenue increased 4% sequentially while operating expenses declined 1%.
Net inflows and a 6.0% rise in average AUM; net market losses reduced AUM by $26.4B and FX added $4.5B in the quarter.
CEO cites 6% annualized organic growth, the 13th consecutive quarter of net long-term inflows, and stronger operating performance supporting balance sheet flexibility.
